bug_description.normalized: When proxy parsing fails inside flb_http_client(), the function frees the request header buffer manually and then calls flb_http_client_destroy(), whose destructor frees the same c->header_buf pointer again, causing a double free on the error path.

source.note: flb_http_client consumes the attacker-controlled proxy string and passes it into the project parser that will either materialize proxy host state in c or report a parse error.
source.description: The constructor first consumes attacker-controlled proxy text by invoking the in-project proxy parser.
source.value_from: tests/internal/fuzzers/http_fuzzer.c:52 materializes proxy from attacker bytes with get_null_terminated(50, &data, &size)

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.note: The destructor frees c->header_buf even though that same allocation was already freed in the proxy-parse failure branch.
sink.description: The destructor performs the second free of the header buffer after the error path already released the same allocation through buf.

root_cause.description: The proxy-parse failure branch contains a manual free of the header buffer and then unconditionally calls the destructor, creating duplicate ownership cleanup on the same object.
root_cause.note: The vulnerable cleanup branch is selected on proxy_parse failure and contains the duplicate-release sequence that leads to the second free.

tainted_value_origin.description: The fuzzer optionally materializes a null-terminated proxy string from attacker bytes and passes it to flb_http_client().

fine_trace.note: Project code consumes the fuzz-derived proxy string by invoking proxy_parse(proxy, c); whether the vulnerable error path is taken now depends on that parser returning failure.

The request header allocation made earlier with flb_calloc(1, FLB_HTTP_BUF_SIZE) is stored in both local buf and struct field c->header_buf, so the destructor treats c->header_buf as the owned header-buffer allocation.
If proxy_parse reports an error, control enters the cleanup branch that contains the duplicate release; only malformed proxy strings reach the bug.
The error branch frees the header buffer through the local alias buf, but c->header_buf still points to the same allocation because the code does not null it or skip destructor ownership.
flb_http_client then calls flb_http_client_destroy(c), whose destructor frees the stale alias c->header_buf and triggers the second free of the same 2048-byte header allocation reported by ASan.

poc.trigger: Provide a proxy string that reaches flb_http_client() and makes proxy_parse(proxy, c) fail so execution enters the error branch that frees buf and then immediately calls flb_http_client_destroy(c).

format.name: libFuzzer input for flb-it-fuzz-http_fuzzer_OSSFUZZ
format.contract: The witness input must be at least 160 bytes so the harness proceeds, select the branch that materializes a proxy string, and encode that proxy string so proxy_parse rejects it after flb_http_client has already stored the allocated header buffer in c->header_buf.

parser_admitted.description: The witness must take the harness branch that actually materializes a proxy string; otherwise flb_http_client() receives proxy == NULL and the vulnerable proxy-parse path is unreachable.
